back: The maintenance of a constant internal environment.
notes: Examples: blood glucose concentration, body temperature, water content.

back: Lowers blood glucose: the liver converts glucose to glycogen and cells take up more glucose.
notes: Secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose is high.

back: Raises blood glucose: the liver converts glycogen to glucose and releases it into the blood.
notes: Secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose is low.

back: Glycogen is the storage carbohydrate in the liver and muscles; glucagon is the hormone that releases glucose from it.
Control in which a change away from the set point causes responses that reverse it, returning the level to the set point.

front: Why must blood glucose be kept steady?
back: Cells, especially brain cells, need a steady glucose supply for respiration; too much glucose damages the body over time.
The pancreas makes little or no insulin, because its insulin-secreting cells have been destroyed.
Insulin injections, regular blood glucose monitoring, a controlled diet and exercise.
notes: Insulin is a protein, so it would be digested if swallowed.

back: High blood glucose, glucose in the urine, frequent urination, great thirst, tiredness, weight loss.
Healthy diet, weight loss and regular exercise, with medicines and sometimes insulin.
